sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 137

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 137:1
items.html: The ten Sefirot of the Mochin of Ima expand in the world of Beriah: the GAR are called the Throne, the VAK are called the six steps to the Throne, and the Malchut clothes in the Malchut of Beriah and is called the Throne of Judgment, Techelet, Sandalfon. For the first nine of the Mochin are the aspect of the Throne of Mercy, and the Malchut is the Throne of Judgment. The explanation: the Mochin of Ima that shine in Beriah come out upon a screen of phase two in the mouth of the Yesod of Ima, which is included in the Parsa beneath the feet of the Nukva of ZA, this being because of the clothing of Ima in the Nukva, and the feet of Ima are found touching the Parsa, which is the power of the conclusion of Atzilut and the aspect of judgment. Therefore the GAR of Ima, which clothe in the internality of the KHB of Beriah, are called by the name the Throne of Honor, indicating the power of the Parsa included in the screen, through whose reflected light all these Mochin of GAR came out. Therefore, although it is a Throne, from the word covering over the light of Atzilut, which is the secret of the Honor, nevertheless it is a Throne of Mercy, for all the Mochin came from the clothing in this reflected light. However, at the end of the Mochin, at their conclusion, the power of the conclusion itself is found revealed, which concludes upon the Mochin, that is, the concluding Malchut. And there all the power of judgment included in the Parsa is revealed, and therefore the Malchut of Ima, which clothes there at its conclusion, is called by the name the Throne of Judgment, for the judgments in it stand there. And likewise Techelet, from the word and the people held back from bringing etc., for the power of the GAR of Ima, which is the secret of the mercy, could not pass through it and downward. And for this reason it is also called Sandalfon, like the sandal that guards the feet from the externals. And it has now been explained that the Mochin of Ima in Beriah in their entirety are called the Throne of Honor, for Atzilut is the secret of the Honor, and since the Mochin came out upon a screen included in the Parsa that concludes Atzilut, they are also found to be the aspect of a covering over the Honor. However, the first nine of the Mochin are discerned as the Throne of Mercy, since the power of the GAR of Ima is in them. But the Malchut of the Mochin, which is the aspect of the concluding Parsa itself, is called the Throne of Judgment, Techelet, Sandalfon. (Items 151 and 152).
